newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Pressure is mounting on Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor to lift his game amid claims his performances are destabilising the team. Taylor's captaincy has been described as lacking authority and he is said to be losing the respect of his team-mates. Page 40.

The New Zealand Rugby League will not consider playing Test matches against the Australian Rugby League national team as has been speculated. The NZRL will negotiate a deal with Super League, seeking improved financial terms, in the near future. Page 40.

The Supreme Court has heard evidence from boxing champion Kostya Tszyu that he left promoter Bill Mordey because he was unhappy from a series of events surrounding his last three fights. Mordey is suing Tszyu and five other defendants for damages from lot revenue. Page 38.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The future televising of sport in Australia has received a boost with a Federal Court ruling that pay TV operators cannot buy more rights to major sporting events than free-to-air networks. One-day international cricket matches between Australia and South Africa may therefore be shown live this weekend. Page 58.

New South Wales has made two changes to its Super 12 rugby union team by replacing Chris Latham and Willie Ofahengaue with David Campese and Michael Brial. NSW plays Natal in South Africa this weekend, and must win to stay alive in the series. Page 5.

Grand Prix sailing will not hold an 18ft skiff circuit next season after a suggestion by the Seven Network. Attention will instead be focused on an international circuit for the new Olympic 49er skiff class. Page 57.
THE AGE

The first game of the 1997 Australian Football League premiership will be played tonight between North Melbourne and Melbourne at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. North player John Longmire and Melbourne's Garry Lyon are returning after long-term injuries lst season. Page B8.

Women's basketball player Michelle Timms may miss a qualifying series later this year to remain with her American team. Her manager has advised her to stay with her team because Australia is expected to win the series easily. Page B6.

The AFL Players Association may take the AFL to the Industrial Relations Court over a pay dispute arising from last year's game that was blacked out and replayed due to an electrical power failure. The Association seeks an additional match payment for each player. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian cricket vice-captain Ian Healy, banned for two games for dissent, will still be appointed captain for some upcoming one-day games. Captain Mark Taylor has indicated that he will step down for a few games to allow young players to gain experiene. Page 94.

The rugby union Test match between Australia and New Zealand at the MCG on July 26 will be a sellout after 20,000 tickets to the game were sold in ten minutes yesterday. Only 5,500 tickets are remaining to reach a record rugby union crowd of 100,000 people. Page 90.

Two of the three leading drivers in the 1997 Australian Rally Championship have withdrawn two weeks before the start of the series. Ed Ordynski is in dispute with the Australian Rally Commission and Possum Bourne is suffering financial problems. Page 88.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The strength of the Super League Tri-series is in doubt through the lack of quality players available to be chosen for New South Wales. Coach Tim Sheens has claimed that injuries and fewer players to choose from may result in a very inexperienced side. Page 104.

There has been a significant decline in takings for the TAB in the wake of rugby league's split competitions. The lack of quality jackpots and the new two-ticket system are suggested as reasons for the ten percent drop in revenue. Page 103.

The Sydney Swans AFL side is facing a tough year with expectations increasing after last year's grand final season. While the side is more experienced and has not lost significant player depth, it has started badly with bookies rating them an even-money hance. Page 98.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
